newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bourse firms, benefits from dlr.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bourse firms, benefits from dlr.

text.p: Hungarian share prices advanced on Wednesday, taking their strength from the dollar, the Dow's rise on Tuesday and from positive impact of economic indicators, traders said.

"Quiet trade on foreign bourses and the unbelievable strength of the dollar principally determined the trend on the Hungarian bourse," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker Budapest. "In addition, there have been relatively favourable macro figures."
The BUX index closed at 5,481.65 points, up 57.59.
Schuszter referred primarily to the GDP figures, released by the Central Statistical Office on Friday.
It said Hungary's GDP grew by three percent in the last quarter of 1996 over the same period of 1995 making the year's overall growth to one percent.

On Wednesday OTP Bank and chemicals maker TVK remained in the forefront of trading with stronger prices, bolstered by foreign interest amid market talk of good first quarter earnings at both, traders said.
Analysts said TVK was benefiting from the PVC cycle.
"I think a rise in PVC prices push the paper's price up," said Peter Postenyi, analyst at Raiffeisen Securities in Budapest. "TVK's sales prices grew substantially."
OTP closed at 4,200 forints, up 200, while TVK added 75 forints to finish at 2,450.
Oil and gas firm MOL shares have been rangebound recently as investors took a wait-and-see stance eyeing MOL's planned new phase of selloff, traders said.
"Morsels of news have started to go through the market and this reduces uncertaintly a little bit," Schuszter said.

A source at privatisation agency APV told Reuters earlier on Wednesday that a roadshow start date of April 21, reported by daily newspaper Napi Gazdasag, was "not far from APV's plans". MOL closed at 3,045 forints, up 25.
But the market was still far from being awash with information, traders and analysts said.

"When corporate results are available..the market will distance itself a little more from the Dow Jones," Schuszter said. "The market always seeks a factor to link to and now there isn't anything else."
"Everybody waits for bigger issues and for the quarterly figures, the market simply receives no other information which could induce a substantial demand," said Postenyi.

Elsewhere, holding firm Novotrade was untraded, while garage services GarAgent traded for the first time in a month and was steady at 1,700 after Novotrade had acquired a 28.94 percent stake in GarAgent.
